fields.claim_quote: $H_1 \cap N_2$ is [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal]] in $H_1$ from [[Intersection with Normal Subgroup is Normal]]
fields.explanation: The local normality assertion saysH1∩N2 normal inH1; the assumptions only makeN2 normal inH2. The actual Zassenhaus conclusion remains true. KeepS3,H1=G,H2=N2={e,(12)},N1=G. Conjugation by(123)sends(12)to(23), outsideN2. Actual permutation group and stabilizer subgroup; normality inH2 and failure inH1 are proved.
fields.flaw: The proof claims that H_1 ∩ N_2 is normal in H_1, although the hypotheses only establish that N_2 is normal in H_2.
fields.witness: Let G=S₃, H₁=G, and H₂=N₂={e,(12)}. Then N₂ ◁ H₂ because N₂=H₂. Also H₁∩N₂=N₂. But with g=(123)∈H₁ and n=(12)∈H₁∩N₂, gng⁻¹=(23)∉{e,(12)}. Hence H₁∩N₂ is not normal in H₁.
